national_news.title: India and China Discuss LAC Understanding and Border Management
bullets: The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) stated that India and China continue to use diplomatic and military mechanisms to resolve border issues along the Line of Actual Control (LAC).
Both sides agreed to discuss ways to improve understanding of the LAC in appropriate areas to ensure better border management and avoid miscalculations.
India reaffirmed its commitment to facilitating the transport of life-saving medicines to Iran as a humanitarian gesture amidst regional challenges.

national_news.title: President Droupadi Murmu Addresses Bastar Dussehra Festival in Chhattisgarh
bullets: President Droupadi Murmu stated that Chhattisgarh is being freed from Naxalism through the combined efforts of the central and state governments.
She emphasized empowering tribal entrepreneurs and connecting them with markets to achieve the vision of a developed India by 2047.
The President highlighted the traditional Muria Darbar during the Bastar Dussehra festival as a true reflection of grassroots democratic values.

national_news.title: PM Modi Congratulates Indian Para-Athletes on Asian Para Games Success
bullets: Prime Minister Narendra Modi lauded the stellar performances of Indian para-athletes at the Asian Para Games across multiple disciplines.
Sandeep Kumar clinched a Gold medal in the Men’s 400m T64 event with a new World Record, marking India's 100th medal at the Games.
Other notable medalists included Thulasimathi Murugesan (Silver in Badminton), Harvinder Singh and Vijay Sundi (Gold in Archery), and Nitesh Kumar (Gold in Badminton).

national_news.title: India Counters Pakistan at UN on Religious Freedom and Minority Rights
bullets: India strongly criticized Pakistan at the United Nations for raising concerns on religious freedom and burial rights in Jammu and Kashmir.

First Secretary Bhavika Mangalanandan recalled Pakistan's historical refusal to acknowledge its fallen soldiers during the 1999 Kargil War, contrastingly noting that the Indian Army buried Pakistani soldiers with full Islamic rites.
India highlighted the systematic decline and abuse of minorities in Pakistan, asserting that Islamabad lacks the moral standing to lecture India on human rights.

national_news.title: PM Modi Inaugurates Chinmaya Amrit Mahotsav Global Sammelan in New Delhi
bullets: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the Chinmaya Amrit Mahotsav Global Sammelan at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi, marking 75 years of the Chinmaya Mission.
He emphasized the National Education Policy (NEP) for aligning education with New India's needs, promoting mother tongues, and integrating modern science.
India has successfully brought back more than 650 stolen ancient idols and antiquities from abroad over the past 12 years.

national_news.title: Satellite-Tagged Amur Falcons 'Apapang' and 'Alang' Return to Manipur
bullets: Two satellite-tagged Amur Falcons, Apapang and Alang, returned to Manipur after migrating across 23 countries in Asia and Africa.
The birds were tagged by scientists from the Wildlife Institute of India in November 2025.
Following a stopover in Tamenglong district to feed on termites, the falcons will undertake a non-stop 6,000-kilometer flight to Somalia.

national_news.title: CAQM Reviews Paddy Stubble Management and Air Pollution Measures in Punjab
bullets: A high-level team led by the Chairperson of the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) reviewed paddy straw management in Ropar, Hoshiyarpur, and Amritsar.
The inspection covered thermal power plants, compressed biogas (CBG) plants, Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVK), and biomass plants to evaluate in-situ and ex-situ measures.
CAQM directed state authorities to achieve thermal power plant co-firing targets and ensure timely availability of Crop Residue Management (CRM) machinery for farmers.

national_news.title: Rajnath Singh Addresses Army Commanders' Conference, Releases Land Warfare Doctrine
bullets: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh urged Army Commanders to adopt a long-term strategic vision spanning 20-30 years while addressing the Army Commanders' Conference in New Delhi.
In FY 2025-26, India's defence production reached a record Rs 1.78 lakh crore, with defence exports touching an all-time high of approximately Rs 38,000 crore.
The Defence Minister released the Land Warfare Doctrine and emphasized integrating cutting-edge technologies like artificial intelligence, autonomous systems, and cybersecurity.

national_news.title: India's Data Centre Sector Growth and Potential of Seawater Cooling
bullets: India's data centre capacity is projected to expand significantly from 1,575 MW in CY26 to 8,000 MW by CY30, driven by AI, cloud services, and digital workloads.
Investments in India's data centre sector are projected to increase from ₹0.36 trillion in FY26 to ₹1.31 trillion by FY32, supported by a 20-year tax horizon extending to 2047.
The Ministry of Power estimates electricity demand from AI and large-scale data centres to reach 17 GW by 2031-32, raising the importance of sustainable cooling methods like seawater cooling.

national_news.title: C-DAC and Bank of India Partner to Develop Indigenous Quantum Technologies for Banking
bullets: The Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC) and Bank of India signed an MoU to jointly explore indigenous quantum technologies and advanced computing for the banking sector.
The partnership aims to create a Quantum Ecosystem for Financial Innovation to enhance cybersecurity, operational resilience, and decision-making in banking.
The collaboration will also leverage C-DAC's expertise in AI, blockchain, and high-performance computing for fraud detection, credit analytics, and secure digital identity.

national_news.title: DDWS Organises Virtual Conference on Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 and 16th Finance Commission Convergence
bullets: The Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti, organized a virtual conference focusing on the convergence between Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) 2.0 and the 16th Finance Commission.
Discussions centered on advancing source sustainability, water security, and Gram Panchayat-led planning for sustainable rural drinking water service delivery.

Ashok K.K. Meena, Secretary DDWS, emphasized shifting focus from mere infrastructure creation to functionality, sustainability, operations and maintenance (O&M), and effective utilization of tied grants from the Finance Commission.

national_news.title: India Exercises Right of Reply Against Pakistan at the United Nations
bullets: India criticized Pakistan at the UN over remarks on religious freedom and burial rights during discussions on an interim report by the UN Special Rapporteur.
First Secretary Bhavika Mangalanandan recalled Pakistan's historical refusal to acknowledge the bodies of its soldiers killed in the 1999 Kargil War.
India highlighted that the Indian Army had buried Pakistani soldiers with military honors according to Islamic rites, while criticizing Pakistan's treatment of minorities.

national_news.title: India and Uzbekistan Hold 10th Joint Working Group Meeting on Counter Terrorism
bullets: The 10th meeting of the India-Uzbekistan Joint Working Group on Counter Terrorism was held in New Delhi.
Discussions focused on countering extremism, radicalization, terror financing, misuse of technology, and transnational organized crime.
Both nations reaffirmed their commitment to cooperate in multilateral forums including the UN, SCO-RATS, and EAG.

national_news.title: India and Poland Agree to Double Bilateral Trade by 2030 and Enhance Strategic Ties
bullets: Prime Minister Narendra Modi held bilateral talks with Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk in New Delhi, setting a target to double bilateral trade by 2030.
Both leaders agreed to boost strategic cooperation in critical and emerging technologies, defense innovation, cybersecurity, semiconductors, rare earth minerals, and nuclear energy.
India invited Poland to join the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative (IPOI) to promote peace, freedom of navigation, and sustainable development in the region.

national_news.title: Sheetal Devi and Toman Kumar Win Compound Mixed Team Gold in Aichi-Nagoya
bullets: Sheetal Devi and Toman Kumar clinched the compound mixed team archery gold at the Asian Para Games in Aichi-Nagoya, defeating Indonesia 151-148 in the final.
The top-seeded Indian pair set a new World Record in the qualification round before claiming the gold medal.
Suvarna Raj won Gold in the women’s F-54 discus throw event, while Swati Chaudhary secured Silver in the women’s W-1 archery event.

national_news.title: MEA Facilitates Return of Stranded Umrah Pilgrims from Saudi Arabia
bullets: Over 3,000 stranded Umrah pilgrims returned from Saudi Arabia to India over a week, alongside 10,000 normal pilgrims on available flights.
Indian Embassy in Riyadh and Consulate in Jeddah established 24x7 control rooms and are actively assisting affected citizens.
Major Indian carriers suspended services to Saudi Arabia temporarily, while alternative options via Saudia and Flynas remain operational.

national_news.title: India and Poland Agree to Boost Cooperation in Defence, Space, and Nuclear Energy
bullets: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk held comprehensive discussions in New Delhi, agreeing to double bilateral trade by 2030.
Both leaders condemned terrorism in all forms, including cross-border terrorism, and called for dismantling terrorist safe havens and financing networks.
India invited Poland to join the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative, expanding strategic cooperation into critical technologies, semiconductors, and rare earth minerals.

bihar_news.title: CtrlS to Invest ₹10,000 Crore for AI Factory in Bodh Gaya and Open Patna Data Centre
bullets: CtrlS Datacenters signed a letter of intent with the Bihar government to invest ₹10,000 crore in a 150 MW hyperscale AI factory in Bodh Gaya.
The company inaugurated a ₹400 crore data centre with an initial IT load capacity of 12 MW in the Patliputra Industrial Area, Patna.
The Patna facility is designed to serve enterprises, government institutions, and technology businesses across Bihar and eastern India.

bihar_news.title: ICAR-MGIFRI Motihari Participates in National Launch of Khet Bachao Abhiyan - Rabi 2026
bullets: ICAR–Mahatma Gandhi Integrated Farming Research Institute (MGIFRI), Motihari, participated in the national launch of Khet Bachao Abhiyan (KBA) – Rabi 2026.
Six multidisciplinary scientific teams were formed to conduct village-level awareness programmes, farmer-scientist interactions, and field demonstrations from October 22 to November 30, 2026.
The campaign focuses on balanced fertilizer use, soil health management, natural farming, crop diversification, and prevention of crop residue burning.

bihar_news.title: Bihar Government Plans to Develop Jamui's Kukurjhap Dam as Eco-Tourism Hub
bullets: The Bihar government plans to develop Kukurjhap Dam located in Barhat block, Jamui district, as an eco-tourism hub with adventure facilities under the Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model.
The project is being overseen by the Bihar State Eco-Tourism Development Society as part of the Unified Eco-Tourism Master Plan.
The master plan covers 7 ecologically rich districts/areas including Paschim Champaran, Rohtas, Kaimur, Jamui, Banka, Nawada, and Valmiki Nagar.

bihar_news.title: Biennial Elections Held for Eight Bihar Legislative Council Seats
bullets: Polling conducted for eight Bihar Legislative Council (MLC) seats across Graduates' and Teachers' constituencies, covering 5.32 lakh eligible voters and 150 candidates.
Saran Teachers' constituency recorded the highest turnout at 13.56% in the initial hours, while Darbhanga led among Graduates' constituencies.
The elections feature 933 polling stations with votes scheduled for counting on October 27, witnessing key political contests including the Patna Graduates seat.
